text: Put the person into the idea: owners, offers and acceptance
description:
Felix 2026-11-11, decided as direction:
- Put the person into the idea: every idea has an owner.
- Everyone can propose ideas.
- To connect an idea to another one, the owner of the idea that allegedly benefits has to accept.
- The hypothesis of a connection becomes the proposer's pitch.
- It should be possible to work on another person's idea (tentative: "maybe"); it shows as "A is working on that".
- Agents are shown on the ideas they work on while they work, so non-human agents get a user identity too.
- The MCP connects to one URL; one URL runs one project.
- Wanted: keep the repository-based way as well (open-source spirit, ideas tracked with code changes in the same repo).

Felix 2026-11-11, later: what is normal in companies must be representable: one person oversees everything, grants others to oversee parts, and they may let people further down oversee certain things. Proposed by Claude, not accepted: you may change an idea if you own it or own an idea above it, so the hierarchy is the graph.

Not said by Felix, open: whether an agent can also own ideas and accept connections.

Earlier, related: db47e131 (2026-10-16) derives "Worked on by" from git authors and co-authors, and already noted that any git user could change an owner field and that a shared git account is probably not a good idea.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: A guest layer tests proposing and accepting with real people before the data model gets owners.
With signed commits an owner in git is proven, not claimed, so the owner rule can be checked by any clone.
An identity that is only a key in git works the same for a hosted URL and for signed commits.

status.comment: Accepted by Felix as direction on 2026-11-11; not designed or built. Needed in the data model, for a repository and for a URL alike: a list of people (humans and agents) in .bowman, an owner on each idea, a connection as offer (pitch, on the proposer's side) plus acceptance (weight, on the benefiting owner's side), and an actor on live activity. Today the hypothesis sits on the parent's side, a one-sided connection counts as an inconsistency, and live activity has no actor. Where a repository and a URL differ: identity is the commit author vs. a login; the owner rule can only be checked after the fact vs. refused at write time; live presence and immediate sync need a shared server.
